extra.message: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput as raw HTML without sanitization. genericInput originates from the user-controlled textarea in App.js (this.setState({ genericInput: event.target.value })) and is passed down as a prop to every demo component. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g. ), resulting in DOM-based XSS.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders props.genericInput (user-controlled, propagated from the textarea in App.js) as raw HTML. Additionally, line 9 injects a script string concatenated from props.embeddedScript into dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Unsanitized rendering of these values allows DOM-based XSS.

User-controlled input this.state.formValue is copied into this.state.href (onSubmit, line 13) and placed unsanitized into an anchor href attribute. A payload such as 'javascript:alert(document.cookie)' executes script in the origin when the link is clicked (javascript: URL XSS / CWE-79).
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput (user-controlled textarea value from App.js) as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS.

Attacker-controlled URL query parameters (window.location.search, decoded with decodeURIComponent and concatenated into HTML on line 24) are stored in this.state.submittedFormValue and rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on line 31. A crafted URL such as /?x= results in DOM-based XSS requiring no user interaction beyond page load. Line 32 additionally renders user-controlled this.props.genericInput unsanitized.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput (user-controlled, from App.js textarea) as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS.

User form input (this.state.formValue from the base ClientSideXSSBase onChange handler) is copied to this.state.submittedFormValue in onSubmit (line 6) and rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML on line 13, bypassing React's auto-escaping and enabling DOM-based XSS. Line 14 renders user-controlled this.props.genericInput the same way.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput (user-controlled, from App.js textarea) as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS.

User-controlled this.state.formValue (set from the form input in the base class onChange handler) is assigned directly to document.getElementById('targetDiv').innerHTML, bypassing React entirely and writing raw HTML into the DOM. Submitting a payload such as executes script immediately (DOM-based XSS).

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders props.injectable as raw HTML. props.injectable is passed from logical.jsx line 68 as this.state.formValue, which is set directly from user text input via the onChange handler — a tainted value reaching an HTML sink without sanitization (DOM-based XSS).

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders props.injectable as raw HTML. props.injectable comes from logical.jsx line 70 as user-controlled this.state.formValue, reaching an unsanitized HTML sink (DOM-based XSS).

Content fetched from http://localhost:9000/inject (this.state.injected) is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on line 29. That endpoint (api/routes/inject.js) returns attacker-influenceable/untrusted HTML (<div onmouseover=...>). Rendering remote content as raw HTML executes any embedded scripts/event handlers. Line 30 renders user-controlled this.props.genericInput the same way.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput (user-controlled, from App.js textarea) as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders props.val as raw HTML. props.val is this.state.injected (App.js fetchData), the response body of http://localhost:9000/inject which returns unsanitized HTML. Rendering remotely fetched content as HTML without sanitization enables script execution (XSS).
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders this.props.genericInput (user-controlled, from App.js textarea) as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling DOM-based XSS.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders the 'script' variable built by concatenating props.embeddedScript into an HTML string (line 5). The script string originates from props that in this demo are hardcoded, but the sink renders raw HTML built with string concatenation, and any value flowing into props.embeddedScript / props.genericInput is rendered unsanitized.

eval(body) executes the response body fetched from http://localhost:9000/inject/eval as JavaScript code. Code received from a network endpoint and evaluated dynamically is dangerous code-injection practice; the response originates from a CORS-enabled service (app.use(cors()) in api/app.js) and its content is served without any integrity/trust check. If the remote source is ever attacker-influenced, this yields arbitrary script execution in the client.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
